poster_title: Adaptive Multi-Agent Reasoning via Automated Workflow Generation
authors: Humza Sami, Mubashir ul Islam, Pierre-Emmanuel Gaillardon, Valerio Tenace
paper_info: PrimisAI, Los Gatos, CA, USA; University of Utah, Salt Lake City, UT, USA

panels.headline: LRMs show promise but lack generalization
content: LRMs excel in sophisticated tasks with high efficiency and accuracy.
However, they often fail to generalize to novel problems, relying on memorized solutions.
This limits their effectiveness in dynamic and complex environments.

panels.headline: Poor generalization and adaptability
content: LRMs exhibit poor generalization in problem-solving capabilities.
Existing systems rely on rule-based or heuristic protocols, limiting adaptability and scalability.

panels.headline: Nexus Architect with IPR feedback loop
content: Nexus Architect: Enhanced multi-agent system framework with automated workflow synthesis.
IPR feedback loop: Dynamically tunes system prompts for improved generalization.
panels.figure_caption: Block diagram of the proposed Nexus Architect. Starting from a user prompt, the system decomposes the task, designs and instantiates a multi-agent workflow, and validates it against provided examples. If performance criteria are not met, failure cases are analyzed and used in the IPR feedback.

panels.headline: Evaluated on challenging logical questions
content: Empirical evaluation using GPT-4.1 as the baseline LLM.
Compared against Gemini 2.5 Flash Preview, Claude Sonnet 4, DeepSeek-R1, and Llama 4 Scout.

panels.headline: Pass rate 66% higher than Gemini 2.5
content: Nexus Architect achieved up to 66% increase in pass rate over Gemini 2.5 Flash Preview.
Nearly 2.5 × higher pass rate compared to DeepSeek-R1 and Claude Sonnet 4, and over 3 × higher pass rate compared to Llama 4 Scout.
panels.figure_caption: Performance comparison between our five Architect-generated workflows and recently released state-of-the-art LLMs and LRMs.

panels.headline: Significant improvement in reasoning tasks
content: Nexus Architect significantly improves the generalization and adaptability of reasoning tasks using standard LLMs.
The proposed approach offers a promising direction for enhancing genuine reasoning capabilities in multi-agent systems.
